redaction: No redaction applied. Precedent: corpus/m2 (same harness family) ships unredacted tool refs, and the capture is free of secrets per pattern scan (0 hits for PAT/API-key/token/credential patterns). Tool refs truncate their argument JSON at 120 characters by design (RFC-0 §6): shell refs are command prefixes, edit/write refs are file paths. Absolute paths (/home/theb/…, /tmp/opencode/…) remain in the clear as in corpus/m1–m3. One ref embeds a /proc-environ read command; the ref carries the command text only (variable NAMES at most, never environ VALUES). No credentials, tokens, or third-party personal data were present.
status: LIVE — first interactive self-capture for the corpus: a long-running OpenCode TUI agent recorded its own working turns (repository-hygiene card execution plus adapter verification) through the v2 promise-plugin adapter inside its own session. Unlike m2 (scripted one-shot CLI invocations) or m4 (Hermes start/stop governor), the trace was flushed at the TUI's graceful exit via plugin unload, witnessed end-to-end by the instrumented adapter (hooks-witness.log).

harness.name: OpenCode
harness.plugin: packages/opencode/live/ctxvm.ts (instrumented 2026-10-25 with the per-hook + flush witness; v2 promise-plugin, export default createPlugin(ctx))
harness.tracer: @ctxvm/node tracer chain under ctxvm-core (RFC-0 xCABI JSONL)
harness.wiring: plugin loaded by the CLI/TUI process (TUI processes carry the CTXVM_* capture env; opencode serve --service does not); ctx.session.hook("context") + ctx.tool.hook("execute.before").hook("execute.after") + cleanup callback
harness.invocation: interactive TUI session (opencode --continue, resumed) env-gated by CTXVM_TRACE_DIR, CTXVM_TRACE_NAME=m5-self, CTXVM_MODEL=opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free, CTXVM_PROVIDER=opencode, CTXVM_AGENT_ID=ctxvm-self, CTXVM_BUDGET_TOKENS=200000; the recorded window contains no scripted prompt — the session commands itself
harness.flush: graceful TUI exit (SIGTERM) -> plugin cleanup -> vm.finishAll() -> writeFileSync <name>.jsonl + .meta.json; witnessed 2026-10-25: cleanup entered -> finishAll -> 1 tracer(s) -> flush m5-self.jsonl bytes=16280 -> cleanup exit (hooks-witness.log). A hard kill discards the in-memory slice silently (pre-instrumentation quit lost one partial window the same day; diagnosed, see packages/opencode/live/README.md erratum).
harness.providerSpend: USD 0 (free-tier provider; the recorded work was repository hygiene and verification, not paid inference)
harness.liveCaptureWorking: Confirmed: the full flush chain is witnessed (see flush); hookStats contexts=14/before=17/after=17/completed=17/errored=0 and the file carries session.open/page.declare/page.fault/page.render/turn.render/call.meta.

files.origin: The recording session's own working turns on a resumed session: the HYG-1 hygiene card (de-tracking committed .pyc files, gating the metrics suite in run-ci.sh + ci.yml) and the instrumented-adapter verification that validated the flush itself; 14 hook contexts over the window, no scripted beats

beats.declare: 17 pages declared from real tool results across three tool families: shell (12 pages), edit (4), write (1). Tool refs are tool:<name>(<canonical-args>) with args truncated at 120 characters
beats.fault: 17 identifier_scan faults — exactly one per novel page, all following the cold-entry double-row shape: the page is declared in the completing call's turn, faults there, and renders in full on the next model request (declare -> fault@t -> render@t+1)
beats.render: 17 full renders, one per page; zero stub renders
beats.error: no errored calls (17 completed / 0 errored); every completed call declared exactly one page and produced no waste rows beyond the expected cold-entry faults
beats.turns: 14 turn boundaries; residentTokens constant at 2055 across all turns (no evictions), headroom 197945 against the declared 200000 budget; netTokenReduction 0.0 vs the counterfactual-no-paging baseline by construction

limitations: v0 tracer is observe-only and has no eviction path (declared => resident). At 2055 declared tokens against a 200000 budget there is no paging pressure, so this drop cannot exhibit page.evict, stub rendering, or second-slot paging; the eviction-shape reference remains the synthetic P-pathology vector in corpus/m1, and pressure data comes from the UC3 policy sweeps.
Faults are deduped per page and source, so repeated re-fetches of one page yield a single identifier_scan row; per-turn pressure appears in call.meta rather than as repeated rows.

The recorded window is the final instrumented boot's lifetime (session.open at boot). Earlier turns of the same resumed session were lost when a pre-instrumentation TUI process died unflushed (diagnosed 2026-10-25; the plugin writes only at graceful unload). Filenames under CTXVM_TRACE_NAME are overwritten by later flushes, so era snapshots must be taken immediately.

opencodeVersion is null in the sidecar: the boot recipe of this session omitted CTXVM_OPENCODE_VERSION. The erratum (packages/opencode/live/README.md) adds that export to the recipe; the value is recorded as null rather than backfilled.
budgetTokens=200000 is declared headroom bookkeeping (T9 convention), not the provider's measured context window.
tokenizerId is apx4-char (ceil(characters/4)), an approximation; absolute token counts are not provider usage figures.
call.meta reports providerReported=false throughout: the harness did not surface provider cache counters, so estHitTokens/estMissTokens are estimates derived from page residency.
The capture is self-referential (the session verifies its own instrumentation) and v0 records page references, not side-conversation content: user/assistant prose is not in the trace.
